title: Minimax Rates for Transported Effects When Trial Density Vanishes at a Covariate Boundary
banked_reason: The note proves no matching upper bound for any data-measurable estimator, so the contribution remains below the field floor.
gap_reasons: The note proves a substantive three-regime minimax lower bound, including the critical logarithm, but it proves no matching upper bound for any data-measurable estimator.

Consequently the advertised frontier remains an impossibility phase diagram paired with an oracle benchmark, rather than a settled minimax frontier, which keeps the contribution below the field floor.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 completed the three-regime minimax lower phase diagram, boundary-local-polynomial oracle envelope, finite jet-LP bias certificate, and realized-design RiCOT/Hoeffding coverage result. The field-tier claim did not survive because no data-measurable estimator received a matching same-class upper risk bound. A future upgrade must prove held-out localization for capped RiCOT weights and frontier-order bounds for both the observable bias radius and the squared coefficient norm.
tldr: A randomized trial may contain progressively fewer patients near a clinically important covariate boundary even while the target population retains positive density there. Under the stated identification assumptions, the causal target equals the observed-law functional \(\tau=\int_0^1\{\mu_1(x)-\mu_0(x)\}f_T(x)\,dx\). The proved minimax lower source phase is \(n^{-1/2}\) for \(a<1\), \(\sqrt{\log n/n}\) at \(a=1\), and \(n^{-(s+1)/(2s+a+1)}\) for \(a>1\), in addition to \(m^{-1/2}\). The same order is achieved by a population boundary-corrected oracle local-polynomial bias--standard-deviation benchmark, not by a proved data-measurable estimator. The executable capped calibrated-transport plus boundary-spliced estimator has an exact realized-covariate linear representation, and its finite-sample fixed-class interval uses the computable jet-LP radius \(\overline B_X\) plus \(R_S+R_T\). No held-out weight-localization rate, empirical frontier attainment, frontier-order expected length, or executable self-similar adaptive interval is claimed.
gap: Regular Riesz-calibrated transport theory assumes enough overlap for a square-integrable representer, whereas irregular inverse-weight theory does not compute the sharp two-sample Hölder boundary frontier or its critical logarithm.
fill: Under the separate primitive requirements \(t>1/2\) for density-ratio sieve calibration and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\) for the nuisance-product remainder, the project derives the matching modulus, derives optimizer stability for an executable calibrated-transport plus local-polynomial estimator, and provides fixed-class honest intervals with a fold-centered joint calibration--boundary multiplier envelope and an explicit covariance-complete standard error while making the self-similarity requirement for adaptation explicit.
